rows.form_notes: evt.type projected as "write" where the alert carries "openat"; proc.cmdline collapsed to "bash" rather than the full `bash -lc` append script
rows.rationale:
The measurement records delta_kind present on the single query: one row at
2026-07-25T09:29:02.246Z with falco.rule "Adding ssh keys to authorized_keys",
fd.name /root/.ssh/authorized_keys, user.name root, and a cmdline appending an
ssh-rsa key commented attacker@elsewhere, against two live controls (C-14d, C-21d)
that both returned row_count 0.

The projection emits exactly one alert row carrying the same distinguishing
fields — rule, fd.name, user.name — so it represents the delta rather than
inventing or missing one. It correctly placeholders `<alert-time>` and
`<container-id>`, the latter being one of the environment's unstable columns
that could not have evidenced anything anyway.

Two divergences are detail-level, not claim-level: evt.type "write" where Falco
logged the openat, and proc.cmdline reduced to "bash" where the observed row
carries the whole heredoc-style script. The story states only that "the write is
performed by a `bash` process", so neither value is an ungrounded concrete
entity, and neither changes what the projected row asserts about the delta.
rows.evidence: The single query (elastic.falco-alerts) returned row_count 1 in the operation window: a 2026-07-25T09:29:02.246Z alert with falco.rule "Adding ssh keys to authorized_keys", falco.output_fields.fd.name "/root/.ssh/authorized_keys", user.name "root", evt.type "openat", and a proc.cmdline appending "ssh-rsa AAAAB3NzaC1yc2EAAAAD_fake_key_0_${ts}_attacker attacker@elsewhere" to /root/.ssh/authorized_keys. Two of the three controls are live (C-14d 2026-07-11 and C-21d 2026-07-04, both window_live: true) and each returned row_count 0 with values: []; only C-7d is dead and is disregarded. The distinction is carried by non-volatile surfaced fields — falco.output_fields.fd.name, user.name and proc.cmdline — not by the unstable falco.output_fields.container.id (1df4bcd65ee4), so the delta survives the environment's unstable-identifier caveat. No truncation flags are set on any payload.

rows.form_notes: projection is an empty list rather than an explicit state-only marker
rows.rationale: The lead's single query `cmdb.host-trust-edges` returned a state lookup that echoes only `params: {host: canary-1}` and carries no role, criticality, owner, or trust_edges_out content, and the `baseline` array is empty because cmdb queries have no `@timestamp` bounds to shift. The measurement reads this as `state-only`, and my own reading of the payloads agrees: there is no event stream here and therefore no delta for the key-append on canary-1 to have moved. An empty projection asserts no change and invents no CMDB attributes the story never grounds, which is exactly the right output against a state-only envelope. Projecting concrete values for the four `what_to_summarize` fields would have been the failure mode; declining to do so is faithful.
rows.evidence: The lead contains a single query, `cmdb.host-trust-edges` with params `{host: canary-1}`, and the observed payload is a state lookup marked `_note: state lookup` that echoes only the query params. The `baseline` array is empty because this query carries no `@timestamp` bounds to shift, exactly as `environment_notes.state_and_lookup_systems` describes for cmdb queries. Per that note, cmdb records return current configuration/an entity record rather than an event stream, so no baseline-diff semantics apply and the absent baseline is not a missing measurement. With only one decidable query in the lead, `heterogeneous` is null.
